purpose: One fixed Game ControllerAI procedure-name discovery query to locate candidate registration/initialization writers for the state lookup used by SetState. It searches every analyzed procedure name internally but returns only the fixed regex matches. No candidate behavior or address is invented; no automatic expansion.

address_sources.source_kind: Saved real Rea SetState pseudocode at 0x180123d50 motivates locating ControllerAI state-registration writers. This name search has no assumed writer address.
Saved real Rea SetState assembly at 0x180123d50, for the observed controller +0x290 lookup and node +0x40 state pointer question. No new native reads.

execution_requirements: Only a separately reviewed fixed Game batch may launch one installed Rea backend. Keep exact Game hash/profile, ownership, descriptor, image, heap, deadlines and cleanup guards; never execute the original, access saves or Steam cloud.

Make exactly one search_procedures call with the fixed regex, mode regex and case_sensitive false. The tool internally enumerates all analyzed procedure names, including external functions, and returns matching address/value pairs. There is no API limit, cursor or range and no claimed result-count cap.

An empty array is a valid discovery result. Names and returned addresses are candidates, not proof of writer behavior, ownership or complete registration recovery. No automatic follow-up, body query, extra scan or retry.

Retain Evidence operation, pattern/mode/case_sensitive, provider, target identity, evidence_id, limitations and address/value rows. Do not substitute caller count or result count for recovered functionality.

Use unchanged Game 384M heap, 5 GiB physical-and-commit launch and 2 GiB stop gates, 330000 ms startup and 600000 ms request deadlines. Past Game sampled peaks are not a bound for this discovery batch.

Require the pinned preceding state-transition batch to have passed, closed, exited, empty Job and exited sampler. Existing Game trial observations remain the resource provenance. Preserve earlier plans and outputs; no tool installation, monitor/security/CPU changes.
